Let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf on a topological space $X$. We say that
$\mathcal F$ is a **sheaf** if for every open set $U \subseteq X$ and every
open cover $U=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$, including the empty cover of
$\varnothing$, the following two conditions hold.

**Locality.** If $s,t\in\mathcal F(U)$ satisfy
$$s|_{U_i}=t|_{U_i}\qquad\text{for all }i\in I,$$
then $s=t$.

**Gluing.** If sections $s_i\in\mathcal F(U_i)$ satisfy
$$s_i|_{U_i\cap U_j}=s_j|_{U_i\cap U_j}\qquad\text{for all }i,j\in I,$$
then there exists $s\in\mathcal F(U)$ such that
$$s|_{U_i}=s_i\qquad\text{for all }i\in I.$$

By locality, such a section $s$ is automatically unique. Thus a sheaf is
exactly a presheaf whose compatible local sections glue uniquely.

Let $X$ be a topological space.
Fix a ring $R$ when modules are under discussion.

A **presheaf of groups** on $X$ is a presheaf $\mathcal F$ such that every
$\mathcal F(U)$ is a group and every restriction map
$\rho^U_V:\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal F(V)$ is a group homomorphism
([[prop-groups-and-homomorphisms-form-category-grp]]).

A **presheaf of rings** on $X$ is defined the same way with rings and ring
homomorphisms ([[prop-rings-and-homomorphisms-form-category-ring]]).

A **presheaf of left $R$-modules** on $X$ is defined the same way with left
$R$-modules and $R$-linear maps
([[prop-modules-and-homomorphisms-form-category-rmod]]).

A **sheaf of groups**, **sheaf of rings**, or **sheaf of left $R$-modules** is
such a presheaf whose underlying set-valued presheaf is a sheaf.

In particular, each sheaf of groups has a distinguished identity section on
every open set; in additive notation this section is written $0$, and all
restrictions preserve the algebraic operations.

Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space.

An **$\mathcal O_X$-module** is a sheaf $\mathcal F$ of abelian groups on $X$
such that for every open set $U \subseteq X$ the section group $\mathcal F(U)$
is an $\mathcal O_X(U)$-module, and for every inclusion $V \subseteq U$ the
restriction map
$$
\mathcal F(U)\longrightarrow\mathcal F(V)
$$
is $\mathcal O_X(U)$-linear after restricting scalars along
$\mathcal O_X(U)\to\mathcal O_X(V)$.

A **morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules** is a morphism of the underlying sheaves
of abelian groups whose components are $\mathcal O_X(U)$-linear on every open
set $U$.

Let $X$ be a topological space.

1. The category of sheaves of abelian groups on $X$ is an abelian category.
2. If $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ is a ringed space, then the category of
   $\mathcal O_X$-modules is also an abelian category.

Let
$$
\cdots\longrightarrow \mathcal F_{i-1}\xrightarrow{d_{i-1}}\mathcal F_i\xrightarrow{d_i}\mathcal F_{i+1}\longrightarrow\cdots
$$
be a sequence of sheaves of abelian groups on a topological space $X$. Then the
sequence is exact if and only if, for every point $x\in X$, the stalk sequence
$$
\cdots\longrightarrow (\mathcal F_{i-1})_x\xrightarrow{(d_{i-1})_x}(\mathcal F_i)_x\xrightarrow{(d_i)_x}(\mathcal F_{i+1})_x\longrightarrow\cdots
$$
is exact.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map, and let $\mathcal G$ be a presheaf on $Y$.
The **inverse-image presheaf**
$$
f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G
$$
on $X$ is defined by
$$
(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U):=\varinjlim_{f(U)\subseteq V}\mathcal G(V),
$$
where $V$ runs over the open neighbourhoods of $f(U)$ in $Y$, ordered by
reverse inclusion. If $U' \subseteq U$, then every neighbourhood of $f(U)$ is a
neighbourhood of $f(U')$, so there is a natural restriction map
$(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U)\to(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U')$.

The **inverse image sheaf** of a sheaf $\mathcal G$ on $Y$ is the sheafification
of this presheaf:
$$
f^{-1}\mathcal G:=a(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G).
$$

When $U$ is open in $X$ and $V$ is an open set of $Y$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$,
there is a canonical map
$$
\mathcal G(V)\longrightarrow(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U)
$$
into the colimit class represented by $V$.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map, and let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf on $X$.
The **direct image presheaf**
$$f_*\mathcal F$$
on $Y$ is defined on an open set $V \subseteq Y$ by
$$
(f_*\mathcal F)(V):=\mathcal F(f^{-1}(V)).
$$
If $V' \subseteq V$, the restriction map
$$
(f_*\mathcal F)(V)\longrightarrow(f_*\mathcal F)(V')
$$
is the restriction map of $\mathcal F$ for the inclusion
$f^{-1}(V') \subseteq f^{-1}(V)$.

Thus direct image is just precomposition of the presheaf with the inverse-image
map on open sets.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map.

1. If $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf on $X$, then $f_*\mathcal F$ is a sheaf on $Y$.
2. If $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf of groups, rings, or modules on $X$, then
   $f_*\mathcal F$ is a sheaf of the same kind on $Y$.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map, let $\mathcal G$ be a sheaf on $Y$, and let
$\mathcal F$ be a sheaf on $X$. Then there is a natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_X(f^{-1}\mathcal G,\mathcal F) \cong \operatorname{Hom}_Y(\mathcal G,f_*\mathcal F).$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$ be a topological
space and let $k$ be a field. The category $\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ of sheaves
of $k$-vector spaces is the category of modules over the ringed space
$(X,k_X)$ with constant structure sheaf $k_X$
([[def-locally-ringed-space]], [[def-module-on-ringed-space]]); it is a locally
small Grothendieck category and carries a functorial injective embedding, and
iterating that embedding on cokernels yields for every $k$-sheaf one specific
injective resolution
([[lem-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]]). These resolutions are
bounded-below injective replacements, so with the dependent choice supplied by
AC ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]) the bounded-below
injective complexes model the bounded derived category:
$K^+(\operatorname{Inj}\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))\to
D^+(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ is an equivalence, and morphisms of the bounded
derived category are computed by these replacements
([[thm-injective-complexes-model-the-bounded-below-derived-category]]).

Now let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety and let
$\mathfrak S$ be a finite smooth algebraic stratification with the frontier
condition of $X$
([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]). Let
$D^b_{\mathfrak S}(X;k)$ be the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ of complexes whose cohomology sheaves are bounded
and constructible with respect to $\mathfrak S$
([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]). Then
$D^b_{\mathfrak S}(X;k)$ is a triangulated subcategory: it is closed under
shifts, isomorphisms and mapping cones. More generally, if two bounded
algebraically constructible complexes are constructible with respect to one
common finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification, then their cone is
bounded and constructible with respect to that stratification.

With supplied bounded-below injective replacements $j_X:X\to I_X$ (and DC or supplied homotopy extensions), $K^+(\operatorname{Inj}\mathcal A)\to D^+(\mathcal A)$ is an equivalence of triangulated categories. For a bounded-below complex $I$, K-injectivity can be tested using only bounded-below acyclic inputs.
A bounded-below cochain complex $I$ of injective objects is K-injective. Assume dependent choice for the countable successive homotopy extensions, or supply those extensions as data.

A cochain complex $I$ is **homotopically injective**, or **K-injective**, if $\operatorname{Hom}_K(A,I[r])=0$ for every acyclic cochain complex $A$ and every integer $r$. Equivalently, $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(A,I)$ is acyclic. This uses the Hom complex and shifted Hom identification fixed in [[def-homotopically-projective-bounded-above-complex]]. A **bounded-below K-injective complex** additionally has $I^n=0$ for all sufficiently negative $n$. The K-injective property itself neither assumes boundedness nor means termwise injectivity.

For a K-injective complex $I$ and any complex $X$, $Q:\operatorname{Hom}_K(X,I)\to\operatorname{Hom}_D(X,I)$ is bijective. Moreover, if $s:I\to J$ is a quasi-isomorphism, its cone triangle is split in $K$: $J\cong I\oplus\operatorname{Cone}(s)$ with $s$ corresponding to the inclusion.

Assume an abelian category satisfies AB3 and AB3*.

1. Every finite coproduct of projective objects is projective, and every finite
   product of injective objects is injective.
2. For an arbitrary small family, the same conclusion holds provided one may
   choose one lift or one extension for each index in each lifting problem; in
   particular it holds under the Axiom of Choice.

Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category. A **cochain complex in $\mathcal A$**
is a family of objects $(C^n)_{n\in\mathbb Z}$ together with morphisms
$$d^n:C^n\to C^{n+1}$$
such that
$$d^{n+1}\circ d^n=0$$
for every $n\in\mathbb Z$.

This page uses the reindexing convention that a cochain complex $C^\bullet$ may
also be read as the chain complex with $(C^\sharp)_n:=C^{-n}$ and
$d^\sharp_n:=d^{-n}$, so that lower and upper indices differ only by the sign
of the grading.

Let $C$ be a [[def-homological-double-complex|homological double complex]] in
an abelian category. Suppose that for every integer $n$ the diagonal
[[def-products-and-coproducts|coproduct]] below exists, and write its injections
as $\iota^n_{p,q}$:
$$T_n=\operatorname{Tot}^{\oplus}_n(C)=\coprod_{p+q=n}C_{p,q}.$$
Define $d_n:T_n\to T_{n-1}$ to be the unique arrow with
$$d_n\iota^n_{p,q}=\iota^{n-1}_{p-1,q}h_{p,q}+\iota^{n-1}_{p,q-1}v_{p,q}\quad(p+q=n).$$
Each right-hand side is the sum of two morphisms with the same source and
target. The coproduct universal property supplies a unique $d_n$ from this
family; no infinite sum in a morphism group is required.

The resulting **direct-sum total complex** has differential of degree $-1$.
Its chain condition is established in
[[lem-the-total-differential-squares-to-zero]]. A diagonal with only zero
objects has zero coproduct: every family of maps from its objects is the
unique zero family. A diagonal with exactly one nonzero object has that
object as coproduct. For general infinite diagonals existence is a hypothesis,
not an implication of being an abelian category. No choices of elements or
representatives enter this construction.

For the direct-sum totalisation of an anticommuting homological double
complex, $d_{n-1}d_n=0$ for every integer $n$.

Let K be a cochain complex with decreasing filtration by subcomplexes. Set $C_n=K^{-n}$, $F_pC_n=F^{-p}K^{-n}$ and $d_n=d_K^{-n}$. Then
$$E_r^{p,q}(K)=E^r_{-p,-q}(C),\qquad d_r:E_r^{p,q}\to E_r^{p+r,q-r+1}.$$
The construction gives $E_0^{p,q}=\operatorname{gr}^p K^{p+q}$ and $E_1^{p,q}\cong H^{p+q}(\operatorname{gr}^p K)$. With degreewise finite filtration it naturally abuts to the decreasing image filtration on $H^{p+q}(K)$, with $E_\infty^{p,q}\cong\operatorname{gr}^pH^{p+q}(K)$.

For a cochain complex $X$, define the **canonical truncations** by

$$ (\tau^{\leq n}X)^i=\begin{cases}X^i&i<n,\\\ker d_X^n&i=n,\\0&i>n,\end{cases}\qquad (\tau^{\geq n}X)^i=\begin{cases}0&i<n,\\\operatorname{coker}d_X^{n-1}&i=n,\\X^i&i>n.\end{cases} $$

The differential into $\ker d_X^n$ is the factorization of $d_X^{n-1}$; the differential out of $\operatorname{coker}d_X^{n-1}$ is induced by $d_X^n$. All other retained differentials are those of $X$. There are natural maps $\tau^{\leq n}X\to X\to\tau^{\geq n}X$. Unlike [[def-brutal-truncation-of-a-complex]], these constructions correct the boundary using the cycle and boundary objects of [[def-cohomology-object-of-a-cochain-complex]].

Every short exact sequence $0\to A\xrightarrow iB\xrightarrow qC\to0$ of cochain complexes gives a natural distinguished triangle $A\to B\to C\to A[1]$ in $D(\mathcal A)$. In particular, for every integer $n$ there are canonical distinguished triangles

$$\tau^{\leq n}X\to X\to\tau^{\geq n+1}X\to(\tau^{\leq n}X)[1],$$

$$\tau^{\leq n}X\to\tau^{\leq n+1}X\to H^{n+1}(X)[-n-1]\to(\tau^{\leq n}X)[1],$$

$$H^n(X)[-n]\to\tau^{\geq n}X\to\tau^{\geq n+1}X\to H^n(X)[-n+1].$$

The derived category, with shift $[1]$ and distinguished triangles the isomorphic images of cone triangles, is triangulated. The localization functor $Q$ is exact. Every such triangle gives a long exact cohomology sequence $\cdots\to H^n(X)\to H^n(Y)\to H^n(Z)\to H^{n+1}(X)\to\cdots$.

The canonical functors $D^-(\mathcal A),D^+(\mathcal A),D^b(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ are fully faithful and exact. Their essential images consist exactly of complexes with cohomology respectively bounded above, bounded below, or bounded on both sides.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

In ZF,

$$\mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{DC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_\omega\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,\mathrm{fin}}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,2},\qquad \mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_2.$$

DC here includes a prescribed initial point.

Let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety, i.e. a classical
algebraic variety over $\mathbb C$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]), regarded as
a topological space with its analytic topology
([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]), and
let $k$ be a field. Write $\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ for the category of sheaves
of $k$-vector spaces and $k$-linear morphisms
([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[def-presheaf-of-groups-rings-modules]], [[def-module-on-ringed-space]]); it is
an abelian category ([[thm-abelian-sheaves-form-abelian-category]]), so its
bounded derived category $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ is defined with the
conventions of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]], under the
standing smallness hypothesis recorded there.

The category $D_c^b(X;k)$ is the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ consisting of the complexes $A$ satisfying:

1. $A$ is **cohomologically bounded**: $H^j(A)=0$ for $|j|$ sufficiently large;
   and
2. $A$ is **algebraically constructible**: there exists a finite smooth
   algebraic stratification with the frontier condition $\mathfrak S$ of $X$
   ([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]) such
   that for every stratum $S\in\mathfrak S$ and every integer $j$ the
   restriction $H^j(A)|_S$ is locally constant of finite rank
   ([[def-locally-constant-sheaf-of-finite-rank]]).

These are topological constructible sheaves, not coherent or quasi-coherent
sheaves. We use the shift convention of
[[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]: $H^j(A[m])=H^{j+m}(A)$. A
groupoid local system is identified with a locally constant sheaf only through
an explicit local comparison, which is not made here.

Constructibility is a condition on the cohomology sheaves of a complex, and it
is quantified existentially over finite smooth algebraic frontier
stratifications: no stratification is fixed, and no existence or
common-refinement theorem for stratifications is asserted by this definition.
Shifting replaces $H^j$ by $H^{j+m}$, which preserves cohomological boundedness
and shifts a witnessing stratification nowhere, so the class is closed under
shifts and under isomorphisms in $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$. No choice
principle is used.

Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion of an open subspace.

1. For every sheaf of abelian groups $\mathcal F$ on $U$ and every sheaf of
   abelian groups $\mathcal G$ on $X$, there is a natural bijection
   $$\operatorname{Hom}_X(j_!\mathcal F,\mathcal G) \cong \operatorname{Hom}_U(\mathcal F,j^{-1}\mathcal G).$$
2. The functor $j_!$ is exact on sheaves of abelian groups.

derivations.claim: **The simplicial sheaf category.** A simplicial analytic $k$-sheaf on $Z_\bullet$ is a family $F=(F_p)_{p\ge0}$ with $F_p\in\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_p)$ and structure maps $Z_\alpha^{-1}F_p\to F_m$ for every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$, satisfying the identity and composition identities for composable simplicial operators; a morphism is a levelwise family of $k$-linear maps commuting with these structure maps. The category $\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet)$ is abelian: kernels and cokernels are formed levelwise (cokernels after sheafification of the presheaf cokernel), and exactness is checked levelwise by [F1]; arbitrary products and coproducts are computed levelwise, so AB3 and AB3* hold; the category is locally small because each $\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_p)$ is.

**Coinduction and explicit injective resolutions.** For $p\ge0$ and $I\in\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_p)$ define the coinduced object $N_pI$ by $(N_pI)_m:=\prod_{\alpha:[m]\to[p]}(Z_\alpha)_*I$, the product over all monotone maps, with structure maps induced by composition of simplicial operators; then $\operatorname{Hom}(F,N_pI)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{Z_p}(F_p,I)$ naturally, because the component at $\alpha=\mathrm{id}_{[p]}$ is a bijection onto the data and every other component is determined from it by the structure maps of $F$. Hence $N_p$ is right adjoint to evaluation at $p$, which is exact, so $N_pI$ is injective for injective $I$; explicitly, $\operatorname{Hom}(-,N_pI)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{Z_p}((-)_p,I)$ is exact. Given $F$, choose functorial injective embeddings $F_p\rightarrowtail I_p$ by [F3]; the components give a morphism $F\to\prod_pN_pI_p$ that is a monomorphism because at level $m$ its component $p=m$, $\alpha=\mathrm{id}$ is the chosen embedding, and the product of injectives is injective by [F4] under AC. Iterating this embedding on cokernels and totalizing along the bounded-below index produces for every bounded-below complex of simplicial sheaves one explicit coinduced injective resolution.

**Acyclicity of coinduced injectives.** Let $J=N_pI$. For every $m$ the component at a fixed vertex $\alpha_0:Z_m\to Z_p$ of $q_{m*}J_m=\prod_{\alpha:[m]\to[p]}q_{p*}I$ is $q_{p*}I$, because $q_m\circ Z_\alpha=q_p$; thus $q_{m*}J_m$ is a product of copies of $q_{p*}I$ indexed by the monotone maps $[m]\to[p]$, that is, by the $m$-simplices of the standard $p$-simplex. On the normalized complex whose degree-$m$ term is this product and whose differential is the alternating sum of the maps that delete one vertex (the pullback-and-structure maps associated to the coordinate-deletion operators, which raise the cochain degree from $m$ to $m+1$), inserting a fixed vertex $0$ at the start of every tuple defines a contraction: the internal deletions cancel pairwise and the top deletion composes with the insertion to the identity, so $dh+hd=\mathrm{id}$ on the normalized complex, the augmented term being $q_{p*}I$, identified with the value at the identity tuple. A general injective $J$ is a retract of a product of coinduced injectives by the embedding of step 1.2, and a retract of a contractible complex is contractible, so for every injective $J$ the normalized augmented complex is contractible: $R^jq_*J=0$ for $j>0$ and $q_*J$ is its degree-$0$ part, the equalizer of $q_{0*}J_0\rightrightarrows q_{1*}J_1$. The normalized complex computes the right derived functors of the limit functor because normalization changes no cohomology, and it is contractible, so injective simplicial sheaves are acyclic for $q_*$.

**The derived augmentation model.** Let $F$ be a bounded-below complex of simplicial sheaves with $F^n=0$ for $n<a$, and let $F\to J^\bullet$ be the explicit coinduced injective resolution of step 1.2, chosen with $J^q=0$ for $q<a$. Form the double complex $D^{p,q}:=q_{p*}J^q_p$ for $p\ge0$, $q\ge a$, with $q$-differential the resolution differential and $p$-differential the alternating sum of the vertex-deletion maps of step 2.1 applied to $J^q$ (these are the maps $D^{p,q}\to D^{p+1,q}$ induced by the structure maps of $J^q$ at the face operators, and their squares vanish by the simplicial identities and [F5]). Since $J^q_p$ is injective in $\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_p)$ by step 2.1, the cohomology in the internal resolution direction is $H^q(D^{p,\bullet})\cong R^qq_{p*}(F_p)$ by [F3]; since $J^q$ is injective in the simplicial category, each column is contractible by step 2.1, so the total complex is quasi-isomorphic to the augmented complex $q_*J^\bullet$, that is, to $Rq_*F$, and the spectral sequence of the filtration by $q$, whose convergence is supplied by [F5], has first page $R^qq_{p*}F_p$ with the alternating face differential. A common internal lower bound makes every diagonal finite: $J^q=0$ for $q<a$, so in total degree $n$ only $0\le p\le n-a$ occurs, each diagonal is a finite sum of complexes of sheaves, and no completion hypothesis is needed. The bisimplicial case is the same argument with two simplicial indices: coinduction is indexed by pairs of operators, the two vertex insertions give the two contractions, finite diagonals follow from the common bound, and iterated and simultaneous totalizations agree on finite diagonals by [F5]. For a composition of augmentations $Z_\bullet\to Y_\bullet\to S$ with exact inverse images, resolving first along $Z_\bullet\to Y_\bullet$ and then along $Y_\bullet\to S$ and totalizing gives a double complex whose two spectral sequences are the two compositions; the comparison maps of the adjunctions compose by naturality of units and counits, and both totalizations have the same finite diagonals, so $R(gf)_*\cong Rg_*\circ Rf_*$ with the models compatible.

**Locally split Čech nerves: the local contraction.** Let $q:P\to S$ admit local sections and let $Z_\bullet$ be its Čech nerve, $Z_p$ the $(p+1)$-fold fibre product of $P$ over $S$ with $q_p$ the projection. A section $s:V\to P$ over an open $V\subseteq S$ gives, for every $p$, the map $e_p:Z_p|_V\to Z_{p+1}|_V$, $(z_0,\dots,z_p)\mapsto(s(q(z_0)),z_0,\dots,z_p)$, which satisfies $d^0e_p=\mathrm{id}$, $d^{i+1}e_p=e_{p-1}d^i$, $\sigma^0e_p=e_{p+1}\sigma^0$ and $\sigma^{i+1}e_p=e_{p-1}\sigma^i$; so $Z_\bullet|_V\to V$ is a split augmented simplicial space. Fix $B\in D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(S))$ and put $F:=q_\bullet^*B$, so that $F_p=q_p^{-1}B$ and every map between the $Z_p$ that is compatible with the projections to $S$ induces a canonical isomorphism between the corresponding pullbacks of $B$, in particular the maps $e_p$ do. Therefore over $V$ the normalized augmented complex of step 2.1 receives contraction maps built from the $e_p$, and the vertex-insertion identity of step 2.1 applies verbatim: the complex is contractible, its degree-$0$ part is $B|_V$, and $R^jq_*(q_\bullet^*B)|_V=0$ for $j>0$. As the section domains $V$ cover $S$, this proves $Rq_*(q_\bullet^*B)\cong B$ and vanishing of the higher derived functors, with the unit of the adjunction $q_\bullet^*\dashv Rq_*$ an isomorphism.

**Full faithfulness and the essential image.** The derived adjunction between $q_\bullet^*$ and $Rq_*$ gives for bounded complexes $A,B$ on $S$ that $\operatorname{Hom}_{D}(q_\bullet^*A,q_\bullet^*B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D}(A,Rq_*q_\bullet^*B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D}(A,B)$, the second isomorphism by step 3.2 applied to $B$ and naturality of the comparison; by [F6] the same holds in the bounded derived categories, so $q_\bullet^*$ is fully faithful. Its essential image is the full derived subcategory of objects with Cartesian cohomology. Every $q_\bullet^*B$ with $B$ bounded has Cartesian cohomology: the structure maps of $q_\bullet^*B$ are the canonical isomorphisms $Z_\alpha^{-1}q_p^{-1}B\to q_m^{-1}B$ and the same holds after taking cohomology, shifts and cones. Conversely let $F$ be a bounded complex of simplicial sheaves whose cohomology sheaves are Cartesian. Ordinary descent: on a local section domain $V$ the Cartesian structure isomorphisms identify each $F_p|_V$ with the pullback of $F_0|_V$ along any chosen vertex projection, and the simplicial identity for the two composites over overlaps is exactly the cocycle condition, so the local sheaves $F_0|_V$ and their gluing isomorphisms descend to a sheaf $B^j$ on $S$ with $q_\bullet^*B^j\cong H^j(F)$ for each $j$; for the complex, the canonical truncation triangles of [F6] build $F$ from the shifted $H^j(F)$, and full faithfulness lifts each connecting morphism from the descended truncations; induction on the number of nonzero cohomology degrees then realizes $F$ as $q_\bullet^*$ of a bounded complex on $S$.

**Algebraic principal bundles.** When $P\to S$ is an algebraic principal $\mathrm{GL}$-bundle, the fibre products and the structure maps of the Čech nerve are algebraic, the local sections may be taken over an algebraic trivializing cover, and the descent isomorphisms of step 4.1 are algebraic transition functions. Algebraic constructibility of a bounded complex is checked after pullback to a finite algebraic cover by [F8], and the descended cohomology sheaves are glued from the finitely many local models along those transition functions, so they are locally constant of finite rank on the strata of a finite smooth algebraic stratification refining the trivializing cover; hence both directions of the equivalence restrict to the algebraically constructible subcategories. No claim is made about a naive equivariant category for a nonfree action, and no proper-descent statement is used.

**Conclusion and caveats.** Step 1.2 gives the explicit coinduced injective resolutions; step 3.1 gives the derived augmentation model with first page $R^jq_{p*}F_p$, finite diagonals, the bisimplicial case and composition compatibility; steps 3.2, 4.1 and 5.1 give the locally split Čech descent equivalence with Cartesian cohomology and its restriction to the algebraically constructible subcategories. AC enters only through the injective replacements and the products of injectives of [F3] and [F4]; the construction is otherwise formal and uses no proper-hypercover theorem. The declared extension-by-zero input [F9] is retained as ambient data; it is not visibly loaded by the present route, and no statement here depends on it beyond its availability for an explicit open-subspace model.

citations.quote: Assume AC. Let $K$ be a finite simplicial complex, $D$ a subcomplex and $X=|K|\setminus|D|$. Let $X$ be a topological space ([[def-topological-space]]) and let $A$ be a
set. A function $f:U\to A$ on an open subset $U\subseteq X$ is **locally
constant** when every $x\in U$ has an open neighbourhood $V\subseteq U$ with
$x\in V$ on which $f$ is constant. Let $A_{\mathrm{pt}}$ be the **constant
presheaf** with value $A$, $A_{\mathrm{pt}}(U)=A$ for every open $U$ with all
restriction maps the identity ([[def-presheaf-on-topological-space]]), and let
$$A_X:=aA_{\mathrm{pt}}$$
be its sheafification ([[def-sheafification]]), the **constant sheaf** with
value $A$ on $X$. Then:

1. the assignment $\underline A_{\mathrm{loc}}(U):=\{f:U\to A\text{ locally
   constant}\}$, with the usual restriction maps, is a sheaf of sets on $X$, and
   for every $x\in X$ evaluation at $x$ is a canonical bijection
   $\underline A_{\mathrm{loc},x}\cong A$
   ([[lem-locally-constant-functions-form-a-sheaf]]);
2. there is a canonical isomorphism of sheaves of sets
   $$\theta:A_X\longrightarrow\underline A_{\mathrm{loc}}$$
   such that for every open $U\subseteq X$ and every $a\in A$ the section
   $\theta_U(\eta_{U}(a))$ is the constant function with value $a$, where
   $\eta:A_{\mathrm{pt}}\to A_X$ is the sheafification map;
3. if $A$ is an abelian group, then $A_{\mathrm{pt}}$ with its group operation is
   a presheaf of abelian groups ([[def-presheaf-of-groups-rings-modules]]) and
   $\underline A_{\mathrm{loc}}$ with pointwise addition is a sheaf of abelian
   groups ([[thm-abelian-sheaves-form-abelian-category]]); the maps
   $a\mapsto\text{the constant function with value }a$ are group homomorphisms,
   and the group structures transported along the bijections $\theta_U$ make
   $A_X$ a sheaf of abelian groups for which every $\eta_U$ and every $\theta_U$
   is a group homomorphism.

Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion of an open subspace, and let
$\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on $U$.

For an open set $V \subseteq X$, define
$$(j_!\mathcal F)(V) := \left\{ s\in \mathcal F(V\cap U): \operatorname{Supp}(s)\text{ is closed in }V \right\}.$$
Equivalently, $s$ lies in $(j_!\mathcal F)(V)$ exactly when for every
$x\in V\setminus U$ there exists an open neighbourhood $W_x \subseteq V$ with
$$
s|_{W_x\cap U}=0.
$$

Restriction maps are inherited from $\mathcal F$, so $j_!\mathcal F$ is a
subsheaf of $j_*\mathcal F$. When $V \subseteq U$, the support condition is
vacuous and
$$
(j_!\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal F(V).
$$

This is the **extension by zero** of $\mathcal F$ along $j$. It is distinct in
general from the ordinary direct image $j_*\mathcal F$.

derivations.claim: The face poset is $P=\{v_0,v_1,e\}$ with $v_0\le e$ and $v_1\le e$, and every strict chain has length at most one. The incidence cochain model for the derived inverse limit of the diagram $(V_0,V_1,V_e,u_0,u_1)$ is the two-term complex with $C^0=V_0\oplus V_1\oplus V_e$, $C^1=V_e\oplus V_e$ and differential $d(v_0,v_1,w)=(w-u_0v_0,\,w-u_1v_1)$; by [F1] the cohomology of this complex is the actual derived global sections of $F$, so $R^i\Gamma(X,F)$ vanishes outside degrees $0$ and $1$.

In the new coordinates the differential is $d(t,v_0,v_1)=(u_1v_1-u_0v_0,\,t)$, which is the direct sum of the identity map $C\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}C$ and the two-term complex $[V_0\oplus V_1\xrightarrow{u_0-u_1}V_e]$ up to the harmless sign in the last coordinate. The identity summand is contractible, so $R^i\Gamma(X,F)\cong H^i[V_0\oplus V_1\xrightarrow{u_0-u_1}V_e]$ in degrees $0$ and $1$ and is zero in all other degrees.

For the constant sheaf $F=k_X$ we have $V_0=V_1=V_e=k$ with both generization maps the identity by [F2], so the difference map $k\oplus k\to k$ is surjective with kernel the diagonal copy of $k$; hence $H^0=k$ and $H^1=0$, and all higher cohomology vanishes by step 2.1.
